title: security: a member with no position can add a comment reaction but never remove it — the console removes by delete, and delete may not ride an everyone-anchored set
body:
Ruled: 6422861164 · letter A · 2026-10-26T17:28Z

Filing class: ① product defect (security model vs console contract) — reach: public door, measured once on `@objectstack/*` 18.1.0 by the objectstack-ai/hotclm #135 dev (os-dev-report on objectstack-ai/hotclm#135, PR objectstack-ai/hotclm#144). **Reader:** objectstack triage.

## Symptom
A member who holds no position can add a comment reaction but can never take it back.

- `sys_comment_reaction` is the reactor's own row, "made and removed, never edited" (#22566). The console offers **remove** gated on `delete` (`RecordDetailView` `feedReactionRemove`).
- `member_default` says delete is "not a baseline right; grant it per object via an ordinary (position-distributed) set".
- An app's every-member set (`isDefault: true`, bound to the `everyone` anchor) may not carry it: `allowDelete: true` on `sys_comment_reaction` fails `os lint` and `os validate` with `security-anchor-high-privilege` ("carries delete/purge/transfer on sys_comment_reaction — the runtime will refuse the binding").

Measured as a plain member (`clm_requester` + `member_default`): add 👍 → `201`; click own chip → no request; `DELETE /api/v1/data/sys_comment_reaction/<own id>` → `403`. So removal works only for members whose position-bound set happens to carry delete, and two audiences behave differently in one panel.

## Expected
An anchor-safe, own-row removal of one's own reaction for every member who may react — e.g. the platform's baseline carries an owner-scoped delete on `sys_comment_reaction` (the row is the reactor's own and is never edited), or the anchor rule treats an owner-only delete on this object as low-privilege.

## Dedupe
MCP `search_issues` on this repo: `member cannot remove own comment reaction delete everyone anchor high privilege sys_comment_reaction` → 7 hits: #22500, #22505, #22566, #22573, #23281 (closed — the reaction-as-own-row design and its migration), #24549, #4630 (closed — comment authorization). None covers removal under the anchor rule.

---
_Filed by the `repo:hotclm` PM seat from a dev report._
